rows.en:
So I'm telling the second story, huh.
It's my very best one, so I'd have liked to go a bit later...
Oh well, it can't be helped.
First, let me introduce myself.
I'm Reiko Fukuzawa, from Class 1-G.
Nice to meet you!
Okay then, here I go.{p}
Everyone, do you feel safe drinking tap water?{p}What about you, {b}?
I can drink it
I can't drink it

I see.
Wow, that's amazing.
You can drink tap water? You're not very delicate, are you?
Not like you look.
Kidding, kidding, I'm only joking.
Me, I can't drink it.
Well, it's not that I can't... I pour tap water into a glass, right?
And then I end up staring and staring at the glass.
Don't you ever do that?
It's a habit of mine.
But you'd hate it if something weird was in there, wouldn't you?
You know how rusty, reddish water comes out after the water's been shut off or something?
To me, it looks like blood.
I start thinking, maybe there's blood mixed into this water.
Of course, that could never really happen.
Still, I just don't trust tap water.{p}

What if a cockroach crawled into the faucet and was living in there?
And you never noticed, and went on drinking the water without a care.
Sometimes there'd be oil floating on top of the water, too.
And you'd just drink it without minding.
Then one day you turn the faucet all the way, and a cockroach comes gushing out with the water and goes splish-splashing around in your glass. What would you do?
Gross, right?
I'd hate it.
I'd really, really hate it.{p}

My family goes camping a lot, you know.
My dad loves camping.
And places like that are scary, aren't they?
There's hardly any light.
The toilets are filthy.
And there are owls hooting and bugs chirping.
When the wind blows, the trees rustle and make this creepy sound.
Anyway, it's scary.
And then my dad tells scary stories.{p}

You can pretty much always find a campground beside a lake.
If it's a big lake, there's definitely one.
So, where do you think campgrounds like that get their water?
These days they pipe in proper tap water from a reservoir, but back in the old days, they used the lake water just as it was, apparently.
Of course, they piped it in properly and filtered and purified it.
But still, gross, right? It's lake water.{p}

That murky green water, you know?
The water with boats floating on it and everybody swimming in it.
You never know who's peeing in it.
And people were drinking that water.
But even at a campground, the washing area has faucets, right?
So it looks no different from ordinary tap water.
And yet what comes out is lake water.
That's gross, isn't it?{p}

And they say hair often comes out of the faucets.
Hair, I'm telling you. Human hair.
Say you're washing your hands.
You feel something winding around them, and when you glance down, your hands are all tangled up in hair.
It gives you the shivers.
You wash and wash, but it clings to you and just won't come off.
Disgusting, right?
It's true, apparently.
They say some lakes are famous suicide spots.
Lots of people died there, I heard.
In a lake, the weeds wrap around you, right?
So the bodies don't float up easily.{p}

Then, as time passes, they slowly rot and end up as fish food.
The bodies dissolve, but the hair stays behind.
And then just the hair flows down through the pipes.
Even with filtering, hair is thin, right?
So sometimes it slips through.
Apparently it was like that until just ten-some years ago.
I bet you'd still find it at some lake somewhere.
A place that pipes in lake water.{p}

Gross, right?
When I heard that story, I burst into tears.
I couldn't drink the water at the campground anymore, and I made a huge fuss.
My dad laughed and said it was just a joke, but that was no joke.
It's a true story.
Tap water's gross, isn't it?{p}
So, {b}?{p}After hearing that story, can you still drink tap water?
I can drink it
I can't drink it

...Hmm, that's amazing.
I'm impressed.
There really aren't many people who can drink tap water after hearing this story.
You're, like, really solid and calm... or maybe just dense...{p}

Did you know?
Of course, it's not like that tap draws its water from some weird place.
It's piped in properly from the reservoir, the same ordinary tap water everyone drinks at home.
So there's no hair from drowned bodies in it or anything.
But still, weird stuff comes out.
You know the drinking fountain next to the gym, right?{p}

The drinking fountain where the guys from the sports clubs gulp down water after practice and stuff.
Haven't you ever noticed that just the second faucet from the right can't be used?{p}

It's got wire wound tight around it, cinched so the faucet won't turn.
It's all rusted over now, so the wire and the faucet kind of look like they've fused into one, right?
Apparently it's been like that for years and years.
It's not that it's broken.
Water comes out just fine, and you can even drink it.
But one day, something happened, they say.
And ever since then, nobody's used it.{p}

...So, a long time ago, there was a girl at this school named Naoko Shida.
She was really pretty, and she was always the most popular girl in school.
People say pretty girls often have nasty personalities, right?
But Shida was kind to everyone, and she loved animals and stuff.
She was good at her studies too, and on top of that, she was a great singer.
It sounds almost too good to be true, but I guess people like that do exist.
Everyone said Shida was sure to get scouted by the entertainment industry.
In fact, a few offers like that had actually come up.
I'm so jealous.{p}

And there was one girl who was especially close to Shida, named Yoshiko Tamai.
The two of them were as close as real sisters.
But they looked totally different.
I hate to say this, but that Tamai girl wore glasses as thick as the bottoms of milk bottles, she was bloated and fat, her face was covered in pimples, and on top of that, her breath really stank.
Complete opposites, right?
So you'd think there'd be rumors that Shida was just dragging Tamai around as a foil to make herself look good, wouldn't you?{p}

But no, there were never any rumors like that.
It's not that it had anything to do with Tamai.
Shida was just that much of an angel.
So nobody ever thought anything like that.
Still, everyone did think it was strange.
They came to school together.
They went home together.
They ate lunch together.
They were always together.
Lots of cliques tried to invite Shida to join them.
But no clique ever tried to invite Tamai.{p}

Like, say somebody invited Shida along.
Then Tamai would quietly slip away without a word.
And she'd stay off by herself, all alone.
Kind of sweet and selfless, isn't it?{p}

And then Shida would invite Tamai.
All smiles, saying, let's all be friends together.
She said it so breezily that even the people who'd invited Shida would end up inviting Tamai too, without a second thought.
I guess when Shida asked you, you just couldn't say no.
It was like everyone was under a hypnotic spell, doing whatever she said.{p}

So they'd let Tamai into the group, but even if it was fine at first, little by little Tamai would start to get on their nerves.
Don't you know people like that, who somehow just irritate you even though they haven't done anything wrong?
People you just can't bring yourself to like, no matter what.
That's what Tamai was like.
But they had to think about Shida, right?
It was hard for anyone to say anything, and when they started holding back and putting up with Tamai, Shida would pick up on it right away.{p}

Without blaming anyone at all, she'd naturally drift away from the group and go back to being close with just Tamai.
Everyone envied that so much, they say.
When Shida was that much of an angel, nobody could blame her or talk about her behind her back.
So Tamai never got bullied either.
Everyone figured those two were best off like that, and watched over them warmly.{p}

When you picture it, it's kind of an amazing world, huh?
Like something out of a manga.
But you know, someone like Shida is really rare.
I've never met anyone like that.{p}

By the way, {b}.
Do you think Shida was a weirdo?{p}Or do you think she was an angel?
A weirdo
An angel
Just a normal person

...You're honest, aren't you?
Straightforward, or maybe you just see the world with a cynical eye...{p}

Kidding, I'm just kidding.
I think so too.
There's something not normal about it.
And sure enough, that's exactly how it turned out.
One day, all of a sudden, the two of them fell out.{p}

Well, it was less that they fell out and more that Shida pulled away.
Out of nowhere, she started ignoring Tamai, like she didn't even acknowledge she existed.
She did a complete about-face and turned cold on her, just like that.
But I guess everyone around them thought that was only natural.{p}

After all, it was the way things were before that was strange.
Shida was as kind to everyone as ever, and as easy to hang out with.
The only thing that changed was how she treated Tamai.
All anyone wanted was to be friends with Shida, anyway.
Shida stayed as popular as ever.
Tamai, on the other hand, became more isolated than ever.{p}

Even though Shida had turned cold on Tamai, there still wasn't any bullying, maybe because people were thinking of Shida.
Tamai was just always by herself, looking lonely.
But while she pretended not to look, she was watching Shida out of the corner of her eye, they say. Tamai, I mean.
Until then, they'd been so close that people envied them, right?
And then all of a sudden she was getting the cold shoulder.
She must have still been hung up on her.{p}
But don't you want to know why Shida suddenly turned cold?
I want to know
Not really interested

Right?
It's pretty wild.{p}

One day, it was written up in huge letters on the school bulletin board.
"Exclusive scoop!
The truth about the school's angel, Naoko Shida!
Naoko Shida has been paid an allowance of 500,000 yen a month by Yoshiko Tamai to be her friend!"
That's what it said.
And it came with photos as proof.
Believe me, it caused a huge uproar.{p}

Nobody had been interested in Tamai, or even tried to find out about her, right?
Turns out she was the daughter of an incredibly rich family.
She was spoiled, and she got whatever she wanted, no matter what it took.
Tamai wanted Shida for herself.
So she paid Shida 500,000 yen every month to be friends with her.
What a story, right? Buying a friend with money.
Normal people couldn't even imagine it.{p}

But once something like that got posted on the bulletin board, the school couldn't just keep quiet, right?
It seems it wasn't something they could laugh off as a prank.
So the two of them were investigated.
And they admitted it was true.
Shida was expelled.
And of course, her path into show business was closed off too.
The people at the talent agency were glad it happened before they'd launched her, they say.{p}

But Tamai didn't get punished at all.
It seems her parents pulled some strings.
They probably handed over some enormous donation.
So she got off scot-free.
There's even a rumor that they pushed for Shida to be forced out of school.
And rumor has it Tamai was the one who wrote that thing on the bulletin board, too.
With all that, you don't even know who to feel sorry for anymore, right?
What about you? Which one do you think is more pitiful?
Shida
Tamai
I don't think either of them is pitiful

Right?
Me neither.
Once you hear the whole thing, it's kind of a stupid ending, huh?
Even so, Tamai stayed on at school, right?
People said a lot behind her back, like how could she even show her face at school.
Apparently she got openly harassed, too.
But she was thick-skinned.
No matter what people said about her, no matter who told her off, it didn't faze her one bit.
If anything, she got even more arrogant than before.
It was like she was saying, what did I do wrong? None of it got to her.
Everyone was just fed up with her.
Even gossiping about her started to feel stupid, so they stopped paying any attention to her at all.{p}

And then, all of a sudden, nobody saw Tamai anymore, sitting alone at her desk during breaks like she always did.
Everyone was happy, saying good riddance to someone awful.
Where do you think she was?
She was drinking water. The whole break, nonstop.
At the drinking fountain next to the gym.{p}

Every time break came, she'd run to that drinking fountain, clamp her mouth onto a faucet, and drink water like she was in a frenzy.
And it was always the second faucet from the right.
She kept drinking the entire break, without taking her mouth off it even once.
Amazing, right?
Everyone watched and laughed, saying she'd finally lost it, but then she started skipping class just to drink, they say.
Little by little, everyone started to feel creeped out.
I mean, it got so bad that she wouldn't stop drinking unless somebody stopped her.{p}

"Stop it!
Let me drink more!
It's delicious juice!
Orange juice comes out of that faucet!"
When a teacher tried to pull her away from the faucet, Tamai screamed that, they say.{p}

Other students who heard that tried turning that faucet, but only ordinary water came out.
No orange juice came out at all.{p}

Everyone was sure Tamai had gone completely crazy.
It was less like she came to school and more like she came to drink from that drinking fountain.
She totally ignored her classes, and class time or not, she wouldn't leave that drinking fountain.
Finally, a teacher got angry.
The teacher dragged Tamai away by force while she was drinking.
And then guess what?
Everyone who was there at that moment saw it.{p}

Along with some thick, gloopy liquid, something like reddish threads came plopping out of the faucet.
It was worms.
Earthworms came oozing out of the faucet along with a sticky liquid.
Everyone was speechless and couldn't move from the spot.
"Orange juice!
Delicious orange juice!
I'm not letting anybody else drink it!"
Tamai's mouth was stuffed full of worms, they say.
And she was still slurping up the worms dribbling out of the faucet.{p}

"Gyaah!"
Suddenly Tamai screamed, collapsed on the spot, and passed out.
She was coughing and hacking up worms, they say.
She must have choked on them.
Then she was rushed to the hospital and operated on.{p}

Tamai's stomach was full of worms, they say.
She survived, but nobody knows what she's doing now.
...That's why nobody uses that faucet anymore.
And this is just a rumor I heard, but apparently Shida killed herself.
There was a tiny article in the newspaper about it.
Apparently she drowned herself in a reservoir.
And that reservoir is the very place this school gets its water from.
And they say the time Shida died matches up exactly with when Tamai stopped leaving the drinking fountain.
Everyone whispered about it.
They said it was Shida's curse.
And that's the end of my story.{p}

...By the way, earlier you said you can drink tap water, didn't you?
Does it taste good?
If you think it tastes good, maybe you'd better be careful.
Maybe you're the only one who thinks it's water, and maybe it's really...
Okay, whose turn is next?{p}

Aww, so you can't drink it.
Is it because of that rumor, maybe?{p}

It's got wire wound tight around it, cinched so the faucet won't turn.
It's all rusted over now, so the wire and the faucet kind of look like they've fused into one, right?
It's been like that for years and years, hasn't it?
There are all sorts of rumors about it.
For example... let's see, the story I know is...{p}

Apparently there used to be a student at this school named Ayako Sugiura.
She didn't really stand out, but she was a serious girl, they say.
Plus she was really kind, the type who couldn't just leave people in trouble alone.
It seems she was often late because she'd been showing some elderly person the way.
There was even a rumor that one of those old people later gave a big donation to her and to this school, to say thank you.
And it seems that rumor was true.{p}

She was honored at school as a good, model student.
A student nobody had ever paid much attention to was honored in front of the whole school.{p}Can you understand how she felt then?
Yes
No

She's only human too, so I think she'd be happy to be thanked or praised.
Even I can understand that.
But you know, once you start wanting something back, there's no end to it, right?
At that point you can't call it kindness anymore.
Her helping people gradually escalated.
Forcing your kindness on people, I guess you'd call it. Come on, haven't you heard of that?
People who rush around helping others just because they want a certificate of thanks.
She turned into one of those people.{p}

She'd show up without being asked, butt in on this and that, and when things worked out she'd expect something in return.
And when they failed, she'd be the only one to wriggle out of the blame, so everyone drifted away from her, apparently.
At first, even the teachers let it slide, since she was helping people.
But eventually people started complaining about her, and the teachers couldn't very well let it go without warning her.{p}

But no matter how many times the teachers warned her, her way of thinking didn't change.
Even the most earnest people fall fast, don't they?
People like her are called hypocrites.
Though I don't think she ever realized it herself...
Then one day.
It was after school.{p}

A girl was sitting slumped on the ground in front of the school gate.
I think her name was Miyagi.
She was a transfer student who couldn't fit in with her class, and she was being bullied, apparently.

She was into the occult, and there were rumors that she always carried weird things around, or that you'd be cursed if you touched her, so nobody went near her.
That day too, I bet she'd been bullied and was crying by the gate.
Miyagi looked a little pale.
And the one who happened to pass by was Sugiura.{p}

"Um, is something wrong?"
"Please, my throat is so dry.
I need some water."
Saying that, Miyagi lifted her face a little.
It was deathly pale.
But to Sugiura, the bigger problem was that the one sitting there was Miyagi.{p}

They weren't in the same class, but she knew the rumors about Miyagi.
What do I do? Everyone hates her. What if I get dragged into it and end up bullied too?
And getting thanked by her for helping isn't worth much...
That's what she was thinking, I'm sure.
If there'd still been people around, it might've been different.
"Sugiura, so kind and gentle, even to a student who gets bullied."
She'd have helped just to put on that show, you see.
But the students and teachers all seemed to have gone home, and there was nobody around.{p}

"Please, take me to the drinking fountains."
Miyagi's voice was more desperate than before.
Even Sugiura seemed a little surprised.
Hee hee hee, {b}?{p}What would you have answered?
Yes
No way

Yeah, I thought you'd say that.
{b}, you look like the kind type.
Sugiura answered like this too, that time.
"Y-yes."
Miyagi really did look sick.
Even Sugiura couldn't just leave her there.
She held Miyagi up by the shoulders and slowly walked her in through the school gate.{p}

The closest and easiest place to find was those drinking fountains beside the gym, the ones I mentioned.
So that's where Sugiura took Miyagi.

After catching her breath, Miyagi thanked her.
To Sugiura it felt a little lacking, but she seemed a bit happy all the same.
So that day, she went home in a slightly happy mood.
Walking partway with Miyagi, too.{p}

And then, the next day.
Sugiura got to school and was stunned.

Her classmates were giving her cold looks.
If you ask me, it was more like,
"You're only noticing now?"
but anyway.{p}

They acted weirdly distant, and wouldn't even answer when she talked to them.
Sugiura thought it over.
This has to be because of what happened yesterday.
Someone must have seen me with Miyagi yesterday.
That's why I'm getting dragged into being bullied too.
...How selfish can you get?
What an imagination, or rather, it's amazing how far she could go blaming other people.
Until then, she hadn't noticed at all that she was the one everybody hated.
The little happiness she'd felt yesterday had already been pushed to the far edge of her memory.{p}

So Sugiura stormed over to Miyagi's class to complain.
She couldn't rest until she'd said her piece.
But when she got to the front of that classroom, she saw something unbelievable.
Inside, the girls were chatting happily...

And right in the middle of them was Miyagi.
She seemed so well liked and popular you'd never believe she'd been bullied.
It's no big deal, really, it happens all the time.
The bullying only started in the first place because Miyagi was a transfer student who hadn't fit in with the class.
And the occult stuff, every girl that age gets hooked on it at least once.
The curse was just a rumor that grew in the telling.{p}

Most of the time, that kind of thing gets solved by time, don't you think?
Besides, Miyagi was apparently a pretty funny girl, and good at talking.
I think she could've become the class favorite in no time.
But to Sugiura, it was an unbelievable turn of events.
She had the illusion that her place and Miyagi's had suddenly been swapped.
Out of nowhere, the rumors she'd heard about Miyagi before came floating up in her mind.{p}

Is this the curse they talked about? Her curse?
That if you touch her, you get cursed...
That's what I heard, I'm pretty sure.
Just then, Miyagi, inside the classroom, noticed Sugiura and gave her a big smile.
Just a normal face, the kind you'd smile at a friend with.
Sugiura had been kind to her yesterday, after all, so she wasn't going to get angry or ignore her, right?
But to Sugiura, even that smile looked like a nasty, mocking sneer.
Suspicion breeds demons, just like they say.
From that day on, Sugiura shut herself up in her room and never set foot outside.{p}

"I'm cursed.
The witch put a curse on me."
She kept muttering that over and over like she was delirious, and she barely ate anything, apparently.
Everyone besides herself, even her parents, she suspected of being on the witch's side... I mean, Miyagi's.
And finally, she came to a conclusion.
The only way to break the curse was to defeat the one who had cast it.
She'd really lost it by then, it seems.
She got out of bed and walked off, staggering like a sleepwalker.{p}

Somehow she knew the way, because she made it to the school.
She stood waiting by the school gate for Miyagi, perfectly still, apparently.{p}

"I need a favor.
Come with me."
Miyagi must have been surprised.
Out of nowhere, a hand shot out from the shadow of the gate and clamped onto her arm.
And it was Sugiura, all skin and bones, her eyes bulging and rolling grotesquely.
What's going on, all of a sudden...?
I bet that's what Miyagi thought.
After all, when she'd gone to visit Sugiura, she'd been sent away.
Without even waiting for Miyagi's answer, Sugiura started walking, yanking her along by the arm.{p}

She wasn't staggering anymore.
She was marching along with firm, steady steps.{p}

Where Sugiura took Miyagi was a reservoir a little way from the school.
And when the two of them stood side by side on top of its embankment...☆{p}

"Eeeeeeeeeeeeeeek☆"
Sugiura shoved Miyagi off it with all her might.
Where in that wasted body did she find that kind of strength...?
Miyagi seemed to struggle for a while, but eventually she sank under the water.{p}

"I did it!
I defeated the wicked witch!"
Only Sugiura's shrill laughter echoed.
Someone who heard it came running and pinned Sugiura down, apparently.{p}

In the end, Miyagi's body was never recovered.
It sank where the algae and water weeds grow thick, and supposedly not even divers can get close...
As for Sugiura, I heard they put her in a hospital.
They say there's no chance she'll ever be released.{p}

And so, ever since around the time of that incident, they say strange water comes out of the second faucet from the right at those drinking fountains beside the gym.
Smelly water, mixed with mud and sand.
There's nothing wrong with the pipes at all, and the other faucets give normal water...
They tried replacing the faucet, but nothing changed.
Only the second faucet from the right runs muddy water, they say.{p}

The only thing anyone could think of was that the water for those faucets was piped in from the reservoir where Miyagi sank.
So people were whispering that it had to be Miyagi's grudge, her curse.{p}

If you ask me, she should've just taken it out on Sugiura directly.
But it was creepy enough that the teachers sealed the faucet.
Miyagi's body...?
I bet it's still down in the water, don't you think?{p}

Hee hee hee, what's wrong?
Are you scared?
Ha ha ha, relax.
They don't take water from that reservoir anymore.
A big dam got built a while back, remember?
Though there's no guarantee nobody's died there.
Yeah, the water source changed, so maybe no more muddy water.
Maybe I'll go unseal that faucet later.
Don't tell anyone else, okay?
Hee hee hee.
That's the end of my story.
...Who's next?{p}

Hmm, {b}, you're surprisingly firm.
I thought you were the type who can't say no when someone's counting on you.
Sorry, don't be mad.
I didn't mean anything by it, I just said what I was thinking.
Same as you, {b}, Sugiura gave that answer back then.
"No way. If I get mixed up with someone like you, they'll bully me too!"
With that, she shook off Miyagi's hand.
"Wait, please."
Miyagi clung desperately to the hem of Sugiura's skirt.
"Let go of me!"
Sugiura tore the hand away and ran off.{p}

When she got home, she happened to look and saw the creases left in her skirt hem where Miyagi had grabbed it.
Even Sugiura had trouble sleeping that night, it seems.{p}

And then, the next day.
Maybe it was bugging her, because she headed to school earlier than usual.
Out on the field, morning practice was just wrapping up.
What was going on?
There was a commotion over by the gym.
Everyone was running over...
Sugiura found herself walking faster too.
She had a bad feeling, you see.{p}

Where the students had gathered was... the drinking fountains beside the gym.
She could hear girls screaming and sobbing, too.
Sugiura pushed through the crowd to the front.

There lay Miyagi's body, dead with her eyes still open!
The faucet had been left running, and the whole area was soaking wet.
The cause of death was shock from an attack of a chronic illness.
That's why she'd looked so pale when she met Sugiura.
Apparently, after Sugiura went home, Miyagi made it here on her own, but had an attack before she could even get a sip down.
Sugiura seemed to feel a little responsible, and for a while after that she kept a low profile, apparently.{p}

Once things got like that, of course, the one who got more and more uneasy was Sugiura.
She was scared every single day... what if Miyagi was coming out because she held a grudge against her?
After classes she went home as fast as she could, and she wouldn't go anywhere near those fountains.
Even so, hearing the rumors still got to her, and she transferred schools like she was running away, apparently.{p}

After Sugiura left this school, a new rumor spread about those fountains.
It was about a girl's ghost again, but this time an awful lot of people actually saw it.{p}

There's a girl wearing this school's uniform, see,
"Please forgive me, it was my fault."
and she keeps apologizing like that, desperately, they say.
Wrapped in a blazing red light, she suddenly lets out a weird shriek and vanishes.{p}

You know, I have an idea who that girl is.
Who? Sugiura, the one who transferred, of course.
Hee hee hee, officially it was a transfer, but actually, she'd killed herself, apparently.
Maybe her guilty conscience was tormenting her...
She was more of a coward than she looked, huh?{p}

Someone thought there was a fire and called it in, and the police and firefighters rushed over right away, but it was already too late.
Right in front of their eyes, the flames burned up Sugiura and nothing else, then just faded away.{p}

But because it was so shocking, and because it came right after Miyagi's incident, the school made it out to be a transfer.
Oh yeah, there was one more rumor.{p}
About that second faucet from the right at the drinking fountains beside the gym: up until then, it was just that the water got left running... that kind of thing, right?{p}

Weird, right?
That got blamed on Miyagi's ghost too, though.
The students made such a fuss that the school sealed the faucet, to do it before the truth about Sugiura got out.
After that, the girl's ghost stopped appearing too, and only the rumor stayed behind, like a legend.
Huh? How come I know so much about it?{p}

Heh heh, my mom graduated from here.
She was Sugiura's classmate.
And while I'm at it, my big sister graduated from here too.
And the one who saw Sugiura burning and called it in was my dad.
They got together because of what happened with Miyagi and Sugiura...
You can't call it romantic, but they're a pretty unusual couple, huh?
These days the rumor's almost forgotten, but that faucet's still sealed.
Phew, that's as far as my story goes.
Who are you picking next?{p}

Sugiura was really happy about the elderly person's gratitude, but she didn't quite get why everyone was praising her so much.
Because to her, being kind to people was only natural.
She'd convinced herself that everyone else thought the same way she did.
Even though they say most people can't do what's only natural.
After that, Sugiura went on being a kind, caring person, they say.
Seeing that, more and more people sang her praises.
But it wasn't only humans who came clinging to that kindness of hers.{p}

Inside the gym storeroom, two children...
A big brother and his little sister, maybe?
...were crouched down, as if hiding behind the mats.
"W... water... we want water..."
The children, in ragged clothes, stretched out their skinny hands, pleading desperately.
How on earth had they gotten in, and why were they dressed like that?
Lots of things were strange, but she didn't really mind.
Feeling sorry for them came first, I guess.
"All right.
Wait just a moment."
Sugiura wanted to give these poor siblings a drink of water.{p}What do you think she did?
She went and got them some water
She took them to the fountains

After hurrying over to the fountains, she realized she had nothing to carry the water in.
"What do I do?"
For now, she decided to go back to the storeroom.
Besides, bringing the two of them along would be faster, right?{p}

Inside the gym storeroom, the little siblings were waiting for Sugiura.
"Sorry.
I couldn't bring any water.
But I'll take you to where the water is right now, okay?"
With that, she picked up the little sister in her arms, took the big brother by the hand, and headed for the fountains.{p}

The siblings were slurping her blood, their throats gulping.
The children's bodies, so light just moments ago, gradually grew heavier...
Sugiura couldn't stay on her feet and collapsed right there.
Even then, the two siblings wouldn't let go of her.
Not until they'd sucked out every last drop of her blood.{p}

When she was found, her body was dry and shriveled up like a mummy.
The one who found her was a classmate of Sugiura's, but by the time that student got there, the siblings were gone.
The student only heard the voices of little children.
"That was yummy, wasn't it, big brother?"
"Yeah, it was yummy."
Like that.{p}

...These siblings, see, seem to be the ghosts that are rumored to appear in this school.
Supposedly they're earthbound spirits who died around here during the war.
Sugiura was kind even to ghosts, huh.
But dying because of it... it feels like something's wrong with the world.
From that day on, a thick, reddish-brown liquid started coming out of the second faucet from the right at the drinking fountains beside the gym.
The other faucets are perfectly fine.
They checked the pipes too, but found nothing wrong.
Some students made a fuss that it might be blood, so the school apparently had no choice but to seal the faucet.{p}

But why the second one from the right, I wonder?
Apparently that's about where Sugiura was lying when she collapsed, so maybe that's why.
And you know, there was a kid who heard this story before and tried to turn on that faucet, but in the end they got scared and gave up.
That kid says they saw the faint figure of a girl in a sailor uniform, overlapping that second faucet.
Apparently the faucet was right where the girl's wrist was.
Everyone was whispering about it.
That's Sugiura.
Sugiura can't understand that she's dead, so she keeps showing up.
Sorry.
That story's going to make tap water even harder to drink, huh.
That's the end of my story.
Okay, whose turn is next?{p}

Sugiura thought it over.
Instead of going to get water and coming back again, she could get these kids a drink faster if she took them to the drinking fountain.
There was a chance a teacher or some other student would find them, but she decided this was the best way.
"I'll take you somewhere with water right now, okay?"
With that, she picked up the little sister in her arms, took the big brother by the hand, and headed for the drinking fountain.{p}

The closest one from there is the drinking fountain beside the gym, right?
Maybe because they were so thin, both kids were really light.
So she got to the fountain in no time.
"There you go, drink as much as you want."
Sugiura put down the child she'd been carrying and turned the faucet.{p}

Clear water came gushing out.
The kids happily touched the water and gulped it down.
As she watched them, a thought that hadn't bothered her before came into Sugiura's head.
Whose kids are these, anyway...?
And what's with these old-fashioned clothes...?
"Hey, where are you two from?"
The kids, who'd been drinking until then, turned around to her and smiled.{p}

After that, Sugiura never saw that brother and sister again.
...You know, it seems this brother and sister are the ghosts people say haunt this school.
Supposedly, they're earthbound spirits who died around here during the war.
Sugiura was kind even to ghosts, huh.
And from that day on, they say not a single drop of water comes out of that second faucet from the right.
The other faucets are perfectly fine.
There was nothing wrong with the water main or the pipes, either.{p}

Instead of water, dry air comes flowing out, and you can hear people's voices.
It apparently changes from time to time, but it's mostly screams and moans.
One teacher heard those voices, and it was decided they must be the voices of people from the war.
That teacher's retired now, but they'd lived through the war.
It wasn't really doing any harm, but they couldn't just leave it like that, so in the end the teachers sealed the faucet.{p}

I mean, it's creepy, after all.
A faucet that makes ghost voices... right?
Hee hee hee...
That's the end of my story.
Now, whose turn is it next?{p}

You can't drink it after all, can you?
I get it.
Speaking of which, it was a big topic a little while ago, remember?
About how sanitary the water tanks in apartment buildings and office buildings are...
Honestly, I figure tap water is, well, reasonably safe, I guess.
Whether you can bring yourself to drink it is another matter.{p}

So, you know about the storage tanks that hold tap water, right?
Regular houses don't usually have them, but almost every office building or apartment building does.
From what I heard, there are places where nobody's been looking after them properly.
Nobody had cleaned inside the tanks, and something like water scale was caked on thick.
In the worst places, the lids hadn't been closed properly, and they found the bodies of rats and crows that had gotten inside.
And supposedly those crows had had their color bleached out by the chlorine...{p}

Well, it's only something I heard, so I don't know how much of it is true.
Anyway, apparently there's a rule that storage tanks have to be cleaned a few times a month.
But there really are places where the cleaning isn't done properly.
The people using that water did think it smelled funny, or that something seemed to be mixed in it.
But they sure never imagined it was anything like that.
Talk about a blind spot, huh.{p}

If the problem isn't the tap water itself but everything around it, there's nothing you can do, right?
And it got me thinking, people are surprisingly tough creatures.
I thought we were delicate, but a little something like that doesn't hurt us at all.
I mean, we're talking rat and crow extract, you know?{p}

Hmm.
But even if I tell myself people sure are tough, if someone asked whether I could drink that water...
And actually, weird things come out of this school's taps, too.
Things that don't normally come out of a tap.{p}

Did you know?
Of course, that tap isn't drawing water from anywhere weird.
It's piped in properly from the reservoir, the same ordinary tap water everyone drinks at home.
So there's no hair from drowned bodies in it or anything.
But still, they come out. Weird things.{p}

It's got wire wound tight around it so the faucet can't be turned.
It's all rusted over now, so the wire and the faucet kind of look like they've fused into one.
Apparently it's been like that for years now.
And the reason why is...{p}

A long time ago, there was a girl named Shigeko Ohara, a second-year at the time.
She was really high-strung.
For drinking water, she only drank store-bought mineral water, of course.
If her hand touched anything, she'd scrub it with soap, and she'd cover doorknobs with a tissue or a handkerchief before grabbing them. That's how she was.
I guess you'd call it a severe cleanliness obsession.
What an exhausting girl, seriously.
It was the summer of her second year...{p}

That year, the record for the most days without a single drop of rain just kept getting broken, again and again.
It was hot no matter what you did or where you were...
Back then, air conditioners probably weren't very common yet, so it must have been rough in all kinds of ways.
And of course, they even had timed water cutoffs, the kind they don't do even in a heat wave unless things get really bad.{p}

Even sunflowers and morning glories, which are supposed to handle heat, looked ready to shrivel up any minute.
There was barely enough water for people to drink, so there was no way they had water to give plants.
I also heard there were swarms of mosquitoes and mosquito coils sold like crazy.
That's how terrible that summer was.
So, you know how every July the whole school weeds the school grounds?
Yeah, it's the yearly event right before summer vacation.{p}

Her class was in charge of the athletic field.
At first, everyone was weeding and chatting happily, but she gradually started feeling sick.
From her symptoms, it looked like sunstroke.
When a classmate couldn't stand to watch anymore and tried to take her to the nurse's office, she said,
"I'm fine. I can go by myself..."
and walked off, staggering a little.
In front of her eyes, everything swirled and rippled, and her body seemed to float up with the heat haze rising from the ground, ready to turn into vapor at any moment.
"I want some water..."
Her throat was so parched that the membranes stuck together and she couldn't even swallow her spit.
By then, she was already dehydrated.{p}

Then she noticed a row of taps beside the gym.
"Water like that...
I-I can't drink that..."
But she couldn't stop thinking about it.
How good it would feel to gulp down the water gushing from the faucet, as if she were bathing in it...
All her fussing about water up till now suddenly seemed kind of pathetic.{p}

"I don't have a choice anymore..."
She finally made it to the tap, turned the faucet, and slurped as hard as she could.
"Gulp, gulp."
But all of a sudden, she felt a cold sweat break out.{p}

"Something's wrong..."
She could tell something squirming had gotten into her mouth.
"Th-this isn't water☆"
She jerked her mouth away from the faucet.
But she'd been slurping from it so hard that she'd apparently swallowed a lot of it.{p}

"Ugh."
She looked, and countless ants were pouring out of the faucet!
The water was cut off right at that moment, you see.
The cutoff had gone on a really long time, and the storage tank that draws from the reservoir was empty, so no water could come out.
What she'd swallowed instead were countless ants that had gotten into that empty tank!{p}

"Hurk! Hurrrk!"
She shoved her hand into her mouth, trying to get out the ants she'd swallowed.
But ants are tiny, so there's no way that would get them out.
The ants that got into her throat bit into the membranes without mercy.
She clawed at her throat and writhed around in agony.
No, maybe even more than the bites, she'd already panicked the moment she swallowed them.
The ants that couldn't get into her mouth crawled into her hair and under her clothes...{p}

Luckily, a teacher found her, and she was taken to the hospital.
The ant bites weren't that bad, apparently, but the mental shock was huge, so her hospital stay dragged on.
She could hardly drink any water, and she depended on an IV drip every day.
Because whenever she saw water, she saw phantom ants...
Then one day, she disappeared from the hospital.
And as for where she'd gone...{p}

She was found in the storage tank that fed the tap where it happened.
The way they found out was that a student who used that tap made a fuss, saying the water smelled bad.
From what I heard, she lost her footing and fell into the tank.
Huh?
How she died?
Did she drown?
Yeah, I guess that's right, but...
Her body had soaked up a lot of water and swelled up.
Up to that point, it's just an ordinary drowned body, but...{p}

The thing is, she was found pure white.
That's right, she'd been bleached.
Her hair, her clothes, her eyeballs, everything...
Supposedly she'd been pouring in mountains of bleach to disinfect that tank and get it even a little bit cleaner.
The story is she slipped while she was doing it.
They say lots of bleach containers were scattered around the tank.
She must have gone a little crazy.
Putting that stuff in wasn't going to make the tank or the water clean...{p}

Inside the tank, the color slowly leached out of her body, and in its place, water seeped in through her pores.
Pitiful, isn't it...
After that, whenever anyone tried to use the faucet where it happened, pure white ants came out with the water, and it was a real mess.
So, since the students found it creepy, the teachers sealed the faucet.
Everyone whispered about it.
That it was her curse.{p}

Oh, sorry.
That story's going to make tap water even harder to drink, huh.
Hee hee hee...
That's the end of my story.
Now, whose turn is it next?{p}

Huh, so you're kind of a fairy-tale romantic, {b}.

We're human, you know. We're omnivorous beasts.
Humans who come fully loaded with all hundred and eight worldly desires!
The human body is nothing but a vessel for the soul.
Just because that vessel is a little better than most doesn't mean it's an angel.{p}

Well, whatever.

When there's a lot of mystery, everyone starts imagining all sorts of things and rumors start flying.{p}

Well, it was less that they fell out and more that Shida pulled away.
Out of nowhere, she started ignoring Tamai, like she didn't even acknowledge she existed.
She did a complete about-face and turned cold on her, just like that.
But I guess everyone around them thought that was only natural.{p}

It was how things had been until then that was strange.
Shida was as nice to everyone as ever, and as easy to hang out with.
The only thing that changed was how she treated Tamai.
All anyone wanted was to be friends with Shida, after all.
Shida was as popular with everyone as ever.
Tamai, on the other hand, became more isolated than ever.
Even though Shida had turned cold toward Tamai, there wasn't any bullying, maybe because people still worried about what Shida would think.
Tamai just always looked lonely, all by herself.{p}

But you know, Tamai pretended not to look, but she was watching Shida out of the corner of her eye.
They'd been so close that people envied them, right?
And then out of the blue, she got the cold shoulder.
She must still have been hung up on her.{p}

But hey, don't you want to know why Shida suddenly turned cold?
Here's what happened.{p}

One day, a huge sheet of paper was posted on the school bulletin board.
"EXCLUSIVE SCOOP!
The truth about the school's angel, Naoko Shida!
Believe it or not, Naoko Shida has been taking an allowance of 500,000 yen a month from Yoshiko Tamai to be with her!"
it said.
And it came with photos as proof.
It caused a huge uproar, believe me.
Um, this is kind of hard for me to explain, but basically, Tamai wasn't interested in boys.{p}

That part's shocking enough, but paying her an allowance is a shock too.
Where would a high school student like Tamai get that kind of money...
That's what you're thinking, right?
Nobody had any interest in Tamai, and nobody ever tried to find out about her.
Supposedly, she was a young lady from an incredibly rich family.
She was spoiled, and she got whatever she wanted, no matter what it took.
Tamai wanted Shida for herself.
It seems that from the first moment she saw her, she thought Shida was the only one for her.
So she handed Shida 500,000 yen every month to be her friend.
Pretty incredible story, huh.{p}

And as for Shida, it seems her show business debut had been officially decided.
So she didn't need Tamai's money anymore.
That's why she turned cold.
"When the money's gone, so is the friendship," or however it goes. They sure got that right.{p}

We're omnivorous beasts.
Humans who come fully loaded with all hundred and eight worldly desires.
And Shida was a human who had those desires, all right.
Huh, you're asking why?
One day, out of nowhere, the two of them fell out.{p}

Well, more than falling out, Shida drifted away from her.
All at once she started ignoring Tamai, like she didn't even acknowledge she existed.
Out of nowhere she turned cold, a complete about-face.
But it seems everyone around them thought that was only natural.
Like, that's just how it should be...
People said all kinds of things, like maybe they'd had a fight, or "Shida finally got sick of Tamai, huh?"
Even so, not one person said anything bad about Shida.{p}

Oh, is that so...
I was sure you'd be interested...
How boring.
Well, okay, if you're not interested, you don't have to hear it.
And even if you come to me later saying you want to hear it, I'm never telling you, got it?
Just so you know...
I mean, you gathered us here to hear our stories for an article, didn't you?
What are you thinking?
If you end up all frustrated, that's not my problem, okay?
...Oh, whatever.
That's the end of my story.
Hurry up and let the next person talk, why don't you?{p}

When you think about it, maybe she's the most pitiful one of all.
The only way she could get what she wanted was by handing over money...
If she'd worked at becoming someone with real charm as a person, she could've had all the friends she wanted.
In that sense, I do feel sorry for her.{p}

What she had with Shida was a fake relationship she'd bought with money.
I think Tamai saw it that way too, at first.
But as she spent time with Shida, she convinced herself it was true, that it was real.
And then, when she faced the reality that Shida was going off into show business, out of her reach, she didn't know what to do, and I bet that's why she did what she did.{p}

Even so, Tamai stayed at school, right?
People talked about her behind her back a lot, like, "How does she even have the nerve to show up at school?"{p}

There was open harassment too, they say.
People said whatever they liked, apparently, like "What is Tamai's deal, anyway?"
But she was only human too, and it seems she gradually couldn't stand everyone treating her that way.
Apart from class, she was always off somewhere, apparently.{p}

And eventually she started skipping class too.
Everyone was glad, saying it was good riddance to someone they couldn't stand.{p}

Then one day, the students who used the taps beside the gym started making a fuss, saying weird-smelling water was coming out.
And sure enough, that tap water was giving off a fishy kind of stench you couldn't even describe.
On top of that, the color of the water was strange too.
Every tap there was like that.
The ones in the new school building were totally fine, though.
I told you earlier that this school's taps draw water from the reservoir, right?{p}

Only the taps beside the gym used water that was first stored in a separate storage tank before it came out as tap water.
A teacher who got suspicious went up to the roof to check the storage tank connected to those faucets, and right then...
There was Tamai, with the tank's lid open and her face stuck inside it.
"Hey, you, that's dangerous!
What are you doing up there★"
Tamai turned around and glared hard at the teacher, and then she stuck her face back into the tank.
"What's she muttering about...?"{p}

The teacher could see that Tamai was anything but normal, called other teachers, and they dragged her down from there.
She thrashed around so hard they could barely handle her.
And she was screaming,
"You're all trying to take away what's precious to me☆
Why☆"
they say.
You've figured it out by now, right?{p}

That's right, Tamai had always been coming up here to see Shida.
Shida had been shut inside that storage tank.
She'd been dead for quite a while, apparently.
Since it was a drowned body, it had soaked up a lot of water, and there was no trace left of how beautiful Shida had been when she was alive.
Her nails had come off too, and she was in a horrible state, they say.
Judging by all the scratch marks inside the tank, she must have struggled desperately to get out.{p}

In that dim tank with barely any air, she sank into the cold water and died, hoping someone would come save her.
Tamai had kept her locked up so Shida would stay by her side forever.
Even if it meant she died.
That's how far Tamai went to keep Shida as her own.
Maybe to Tamai, Shida wasn't even human anymore.
She'd already become a thing.{p}

From what I heard, the tank's cleaning day fell right around the time she was first locked up.
But the cleaning never got done...
Up till then, the cleaning had only been on paper; apparently it had never actually been done properly.
They say if the cleaning had been done properly back then, she might have been found and saved.
After that, they cleaned out the tank and got the taps working normally again, but...
For some reason, out of that second faucet from the right comes a thick, fishy-smelling liquid, glugging and gurgling.
The other faucets give normal water.
And no matter how many times they checked the pipes and the tank, they never found anything wrong.{p}

Who knows? How would I know that?
Why don't you sneak over later and take the seal off the faucet?
Do you have the guts to try?
Hee hee hee.
That's the end of my story.
Now, whose turn is it next?{p}
